data.name: Boston Jewish Cultural Walking Tour
data.headline: 2 Hours • Ages 5+
data.description:
#Explore the "Back Side"

**Duration**
2 hours

**Highlights include:**

- The Milk Street Café, a strictly Kosher Oasis in Downtown
- The Famine Memorial
- Home of The Jewish Advocate
- The Jewish “Back Side” of Beacon Hill
- Boston’s Historic Vilna Shul
- The West End House
- Puffer House Cigar-Rolling Factory
- The Holocaust Memorial
- Boston’s Immigrant Arrival Area, the North End

##About
Join us for a cultural heritage walking tour through Beacon Hill’s “back side,” where Jews and African Americans resided during the nineteenth century. Visit the historic Vilna Shul in the center of Beacon Hill and pass by Jewish homes and neighborhoods. See the West End House, a settlement house where West End Jews were provided social services, and the Puffer House Cigar-Rolling Factory, typical of the work locales of Boston’s Jews. 

We’ll go through Boston’s impressive and impactful Holocaust Memorial in one of Boston’s oldest neighborhoods and then conclude our tour at the entrance to the North End, which was a Jewish immigrant enclave before the arrival of Italians transformed the area into a “Little Italy” around the turn of the century. 


What Is Not Included?
Food and drinks are not included in the ticket price. If you would like to purchase lunch or a snack at the tour's meeting location (a kosher cafe), please arrive early and bring extra cash!


**Meeting Location**

Milk St near Devonshire St (Boston, MA)
(Exact meeting location details will be provided immediately upon purchase of tickets.)

data.booking_notes:
**Important Notice:** Please arrive at least 10 minutes before scheduled tour time, as tours depart right on time.

**Meeting Location:** The tour will meet at the Milk Street Cafe, 50 Milk Street, Boston MA 02109. Located on the corner of Milk and Devonshire Streets, the Cafe is two blocks from Washington Street at the Old South Meeting House. Your Boston CityWalks Tour Guide will have either a dark shirt or jacket with the "Boston CityWalks" name and a dark blue "Boston CityWalks" cap.

**What to Wear**

You will be outside for much of the tour, so dress for the forecasted weather! We recommend layers, as the temperatures can become higher throughout the day. (It's easy to peel a layer off!)
Wear comfortable walking shoes.
On sunny days, we suggest you use sunscreen. Hats and sunglasses can also be helpful.
If the weather forecast calls for rain or showers, rain jackets, umbrellas and hats can help. On most tours, the guide will have emergency ponchos available in case of unexpected inclement weather.
 
**What to Bring/What Not to Bring**

We suggest you bring a bottle of water with you. These can also be purchased at street vendors along the way. (If you intend to purchase water, be sure to bring some extra cash!)
If you have young children, it is highly recommended that you bring a folding carriage with you, as kids do get tired along the way.
And of course, BRING YOUR CAMERA!!
 
**Other Tips & Guidelines**

Please arrive at least 10 minutes before scheduled departure time.
If there are any particular types of things you would like to see or hear about, please get ready to let your guide know.
If you have any problems or questions prior to the tour, you can call our main number at 866-WE-WALKS. If you need to reach us close to tour time, call 508-904-2819.
Gratuities are not required, but certainly are welcome and appreciated!!
